transcript.text: Just got a new Siemens dishwasher and there's always a bit of water left in the bottom under the filter after it finishes. Is it draining properly?

Yes, this is completely normal. In fact, if your Siemens dishwasher did not have any water left at the bottom, it would likely indicate a problem with the drain pump or check valve.

Here’s why there is always a small amount of water in the sump (the area under the filter):

### 1. It’s Designed to Keep Water There
The small pool of water acts as a seal for the drain pump and hose system. This prevents:
• Sewer gases from backing up into your dishwasher through the drain line.
• Dirty water from the sink or garbage disposal (if connected) from siphoning back into your clean dishwasher.

### 2. How Much Water is Normal?
• A few tablespoons to a small cup (roughly 50–100 ml / 2–4 oz) is typical.
• The water level should be just below the top of the filter housing or slightly above it, depending on the model.

### 3. When to Worry
You only need to investigate if:
• The water level is very high (e.g., several inches deep) and doesn’t drain at all during a cycle.
• You see standing water that doesn’t recede after the cycle ends.
• There’s a foul odor coming from the sump area.
• The dishwasher isn’t draining dishes properly or leaves them wet with pooled water on the floor of the tub.

### ✅ What You Should Do:
1. Leave it alone. Don’t try to remove all the water after every cycle.
2. Clean the filter regularly (every 1–2 months) as per your manual to ensure proper drainage and prevent clogs.
3. Check for kinks in the drain hose if you ever notice poor draining during a cycle.

If you’re still unsure, you can check your specific Siemens model’s user manual under “Maintenance” or “Troubleshooting”—it will explicitly state that some residual water is normal and expected.

Enjoy your new dishwasher! 🍽️
